subject: Decision: secure lane selection for on‑prem LLM (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)

Subject: Secure lane selection for on-prem LLM (short brief + asks)

Alex / Acme NetOps team —

Thanks for the time on Friday. We sketched three viable patterns for connecting your on‑prem inference cluster to Redwood Private: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a site‑to‑site VPN (IPSec with BGP). Before we get the engineers deep into configs, a quick alignment question set so we pick the most operationally sustainable approach: 

- Compliance constrains: can your security team accept cross‑account peering (full route visibility) or must we restrict surface area to endpoint‑only access?
- Expected sustained throughput (Mbps) and 95th percentile P95 latency target for model inference calls.
- Is there a preference for managed endpoints (PrivateLink) vs you managing tunnel termination on a firewall/VPN gateway?
- Any egress cost sensitivity we should account for?

Attached a short one‑pager comparing the three patterns and a worksheet for your netops team to fill in constraints. Can you fill the worksheet and return by EOD Friday? I’ll include Kimberly and Karthik for the security/ops considerations.

Next steps I propose after your answers: quick tech deep dive (30m) with your netops + our infra, then a one‑week pilot of the chosen path.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | +1 415‑555‑0192

Subject: Re: Secure lane selection for on-prem LLM (short brief + asks)

Diego — thanks for the clear summary and the worksheet. Quick answers from our side (high level) so you can advise: 

- Compliance: our security policy forbids long‑term cross‑account peering. We can do peering for a short pilot if it helps troubleshooting, but anything production must be least‑privilege and firewall enforced.
- Throughput: typical sustained is ~200 Mbps, burst to 800 Mbps. P95 latency goal is sub‑60ms for inference RPCs.
- Management preference: we prefer PrivateLink for control plane simplicity but we need end‑to‑end audit logs and mutual TLS. If PrivateLink cannot meet the P95 latency reliably, we prefer a managed S2S IPSec with BGP for better path control.
- Egress costs: moderate sensitivity — high sustained egress will need a fixed pricing carve‑out in the commercial terms.

Notes from NetOps (forwarding):

From: Acme NetOps <netops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:05:13 -0700
Subject: ACME network constraints (worksheet attached)

We attached an Excel with firewall rules, public IP constraints, and our preferred gateway models. We also noted: no additional public NATs; must use existing on‑prem HSMs for key operations where possible.

— Alex
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Smith <alex.smith@acme-corp.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Secure lane selection for on-prem LLM (short brief + asks)

Thanks Alex / NetOps — appreciate the detail. A few observations from security & platform: 

- Peering: given their policy forbids long‑term cross‑account peering, we should treat peering as troubleshooting only. Peering exposes route tables and broad access; operationally risky for multi‑tenant hosts.

- PrivateLink: aligns well with least‑privilege (Redwood provides an interface endpoint per model/service). Verify whether your firewall team can establish SGs that limit traffic by ENI/endpoint. PrivateLink does introduce an extra network hop which may add ~5–15ms — need to test with realistic messages. Also requires us to publish service network load balancers in the region.

- S2S VPN + BGP: gives you full control over routing and predictable pathing; with an MPLS‑grade provider or direct interconnect it will meet latency/throughput, but operational burden (monitoring, key rotation, tunnel failover) is higher. If you insist on your HSM for key ops, S2S lets you terminate on your gateway and preserve HSM flows.

Ask: Alex, can you confirm whether your on‑prem gateways support AES‑GCM + IKEv2 with route‑based BGP failovers? If yes, we can propose a hardened S2S config.

I attached a short checklist for compliance reviewers and a one‑pager we use when sizing endpoint vs tunnel overhead.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference

On Thu, Sep 9, 2026 at 08:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 
> - PrivateLink: aligns well with least‑privilege ...
>
Agree with Kim. Two operational points from infra: 

1) Monitoring & SLAs — PrivateLink means we have to instrument per‑endpoint metrics (latency, token throughput) and propagate to your observability stack (we can forward spans or push to your collector). For S2S we can aggregate at the VPN gateway; you lose per‑service granularity unless you split interfaces.

2) Failover tests — for production we recommend a dual‑path pilot: PrivateLink primary + S2S backup (tunnel cold standby). This hybrid buys least‑privilege while giving predictable failover. It does increase configuration complexity and will need automation around BGP route priorities and route‑health checks.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- Friday (9/10): 30m technical call (NetOps + Redwood infra/security) — agree configs and test plan.
- Week of 9/13: 3‑day pilot: measure P95 latency and sustained throughput; capture audit logs.
- Week of 9/20: decide path for GA (PrivateLink only vs PrivateLink + S2S).

If that works I’ll open a Jira ticket for the pilot and assign owners.

— Karthik
